trades.headline: Sell a struggling Drake Maye + banged-up Zay Flowers for red-zone monster Amon-Ra St. Brown and a QB bridge
trades.summary: Maye is turnover-prone and benched-in-all-but-name right now, while Kyler Murray is only a one-year rental for the partner; flip both plus Flowers for St. Brown's elite target share and a Superflex fill-in while Caleb Williams is hurt.

give: Maye has thrown 4 INTs in 2 games and looks 'scared' per analysts; Patriots offense scored just 10 and 13 points.
Flowers is questionable (hamstring) and is only my WR4/flex depth behind Smith-Njigba, Nabers and McMillan.
get: St. Brown: 19/27 targets, 209 yards, 4 TD through 2 games and leads the NFL with 6 red-zone targets.
Murray is a locked-in Vikings starter who fills my Superflex spot now while Caleb Williams (hamstring) sits out.
you: St. Brown slots straight into a starting WR spot, a clear value and target-share upgrade over Flowers.
Murray covers the Caleb Williams absence this year without touching my dynasty QB pieces (McCarthy, Shough).
them: Partner is QB-thin; Murray is a league-minimum, one-year deal they'd reasonably flip for a younger long-term arm in Maye.
Partner is WR-deep, so moving a productive but replaceable St. Brown for a buy-low Maye plus a flex piece is low-risk for them.

risks: Maye could rebound if the Patriots' offensive line/scheme issues get fixed, making this look like an early sell.
Murray's dynasty value approaches zero after 2026 since it's only a one-year contract.

trades.headline: Sell Malik Nabers (post-Dart QB downgrade) and a buried Harold Fannin for bell-cow Jonathan Taylor and Davante Adams
trades.summary: Nabers' target share collapsed after Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury handed the Giants to Jameis Winston; flip him and a stuck rookie TE for a true workhorse RB and a proven red-zone WR.

give: Nabers: 1-of-4 targets in Week 2 after Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury moved Jameis Winston to starting QB.
Fannin is Cleveland's clear third option in the passing game (17.3% target share, zero red-zone targets).
get: Taylor has back-to-back 90+ rushing yard, 2-TD games and remains the Colts' clear workhorse entering Week 3.
Adams is positioned for another high-volume role and led all WRs with 30 red-zone targets, 14 TDs in 2025.
you: Taylor fills my thin RB spot immediately behind a Walker/Achane pairing that is my only real RB depth.
Adams is plug-and-play WR depth behind a deep room, insurance if Zay Flowers' hamstring lingers.
them: Partner is TE/WR-thin; Nabers (WR1 talent) and Fannin (rookie TE) both address needs directly, RB/QB marked deep.
Adams, 33, is flagged as a regression candidate by Rams beat writers, an easy send in a youth-for-need swap.

risks: Taylor is a true RB1; a 2-0 team may resist moving him even from a stated-deep RB room.
Nabers' dip could reverse if Winston settles in or the Giants find a new starter, turning this into a sell-low.
